the ERP correlates of memory judgments are sensitive to decision bias and to memory strength, and that these two effects can interact in complex ways.

decision bias is reflected in the amplitude of an ERP component that is sensitive to the manipulation via instructions, with more negative amplitude reflecting more liberal bias.

ERPs can be used to investigate the neural correlates of memory decisions, and that these neural correlates can be used to understand the dynamics of memory retrieval and decision-making.

the ERP correlates of memory judgments depend on the nature of the memory decision and the way in which the memory decision is made, and that ERP correlates of bias and memory interact in a complex manner.

ERPs are a powerful tool to investigate the dynamics of memory judgments, and can help us understand the mechanisms that underlie memory decisions.
